query: What reasons or compliance risks appear in declined expenses?

per_column.name: decline_reason_flags
per_column.rationale: This column enumerates the actual decline reasons (missing source reference, exceeds threshold, missing documentation, outside-policy department, etc.), which are literally the constitutive parts of the concept 'declined_expense_reasons'. It is an aspect OF the concept, not an external predictor.

per_column.name: compliance_risk_level
per_column.rationale: Severity/risk level (Low/Medium/High) is an aspect of a decline reason -- it characterizes the compliance-risk dimension the query explicitly asks about ('compliance risks'). It decomposes the concept along its risk-severity facet rather than restating the whole.

per_column.name: compliance_category
per_column.rationale: Grouping reasons into Documentation Gap / Authorization Control / Policy Violation is a taxonomic facet OF the decline reasons -- a higher-level aspect of the same concept, meronymically part of the reason space.

judge.rationale: All three columns are genuine facets of 'declined_expense_reasons': the specific reason flags, the risk severity, and the compliance category are each an aspect OF the concept rather than external predictors or causes. However mutual exclusivity is only moderate: decline_reason_flags already encodes the semantic content that compliance_category summarizes (e.g., 'missing_source_reference' -> Documentation Gap; 'high_value_requires_additional_approval' -> Authorization Control), so the category facet substantially overlaps with the reason facet, and risk_level is derivable from the same reason content, creating partial redundancy across facets. Exhaustiveness is fairly good: the set covers the reason itself, its risk severity, and its compliance type, which are the main constitutive aspects the query targets; a distinct 'remediation/resolution' or 'responsible-party' facet is missing but the core reason-space is well covered.
